## Summary

Added src/agent/ with define.ts (types + defineTool), links.ts (deep links to real dashboard routes), registry.ts (the single tool list), runtime.ts (validate -> run -> audit in finally), and five tools: get_activity, get_board, get_agenda, get_inbox, search_documents. Regenerated database.types.ts so the M8 views are typed. Eight Bun unit tests cover registry shape, the audit write, validation failures still auditing, audit-failure isolation, output caps and deep-link shape. lint 0/0, typecheck clean, build passes, full frontend suite 13/13.

## Decisions

- **Ported the obsidian-out/.obsidian/plugins/ ignore rule onto this branch**: The rule lived only on unmerged task/PSI-065 and task/PSI-071. Without it, git add -A on any branch cut from master sweeps bundled third-party plugin code (including credentials) into the index, which GitHub Push Protection then rejects. This was the second occurrence; the rule belongs on master, not on one feature branch.
- **Treat view columns as nullable in the tools and default at the call site**: Postgres type generation marks view columns nullable because it cannot prove otherwise, and typecheck rejected the direct property access. Filtering out null ids and defaulting the rest is correct for a view and satisfies the compiler without casting.
- **Mock the supabase client with a chainable PromiseLike class in tests, with one targeted lint suppression**: Tools do `await builder`, so the mock must be a thenable; oxlint's unicorn/no-thenable flags that as an error. The suppression is scoped to one line with a reason, matching existing precedent in src/components/ui for rule conflicts.
- **Deep links carry the entity id as a query param to the module route**: The dashboard has no per-entity route yet, so a fictional /dashboard/tasks/<id> would 404. Kept the links valid today and confined the path map to links.ts so real detail routes are a one-file change.
- **Removed `import 'server-only'` need not be permanent: kept it in runtime.ts and stubbed it in the test**: runtime.ts is server-only code and the repo convention imports it (five existing files do). 'server-only' throws unconditionally outside a Next build, so the test stubs the module before dynamically importing the runtime rather than weakening the source.

## Risks

- The tools query the M8 views, which land in supabase/migrations/20260926060000_m8_agent_layer.sql. That migration is on task/PSI-071 (PR #37). PSI-072 must not reach an environment without PSI-071 or every tool fails with 'relation does not exist'.
- runtime.ts swallows audit-insert failures by design (logs to console). If audit writes start failing systematically, calls still succeed and the trail silently thins — needs a monitor if this becomes load-bearing.
